extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in combinatorics/poset theory
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions and algebraic/combinatorial properties of promotion, evacuation, and r-differential posets; includes operator identities, enumerative consequences, and spectral results for level subgraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion operator (∂) on linear extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a linear extension f of a poset P, promotion ∂ is defined by removing the label 1 from the element t1 with f(t1)=1, then repeatedly 'sliding' the smallest label among elements covering the current element down along a promotion chain t1 ⋖ t2 ⋖ ... ⋖ tk to a maximal element, relabeling the last element by p+1, then subtracting 1 from every label to obtain f∂.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure described as sliding labels down a maximal chain (the promotion chain). Figures and an extended example illustrate the chain, the sliding, and the final subtraction of 1; ∂ acts on the right and gives a bijection on the set L(P) of linear extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual promotion (∂*) and inverse relation
rubrics_metrics.description: Dual promotion ∂* is defined by the analogous 'top-down' sliding of the largest label p from some element u1 down through elements covered by u1 to a minimal element uk, then labeling uk by 0 and adding 1 to all labels; it is easy to check that ∂*: L(P) → L(P) is a bijection and ∂^{-1} = ∂*.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: promotion from bottom vs dual promotion from top; used to describe algebraic relations among promotion/evacuation operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evacuation operator (ǫ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evacuation of a linear extension f is defined by iterated promotion-with-freezing: compute f∂, freeze the label p into place, apply ∂ to the restriction to the remaining elements, freeze the next largest label, and continue until all labels are frozen; the frozen labels define fǫ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evacuation can be viewed as successive promotions on the remaining unfrozen subposets. Example figures show promotion paths and frozen elements; evacuation interacts algebraically with promotion and dual promotion (see Theorem 3.20.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic relations among ∂, ǫ, and ǫ* (Theorem 3.20.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a p-element poset P the operators satisfy: (a) evacuation is an involution ǫ^2 = 1; (b) ∂^p = ǫ ǫ*; (c) ∂ ǫ = ǫ ∂^{-1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These identities permit interpreting the subgroup generated by ǫ and ǫ* (involutions) as a dihedral group and link promotion cycles to evacuation; proofs use representing linear extensions as words and Coxeter-style generator relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axiom (D1): graded, locally finite, ˆ0
rubrics_metrics.description: An r-differential poset P must have a ˆ0 and be locally finite and graded (i.e., every interval [ˆ0,t] is graded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the foundational structural requirement for the class of r-differential posets; used throughout for defining U and D and for linear-algebraic arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axiom (D2): up-degree vs down-degree shift
rubrics_metrics.description: If t ∈ P covers exactly k elements, then t is covered by exactly k + r elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This numerical local balance condition (difference of r between numbers of covers and covered elements) is the core combinatorial constraint defining r-differential posets; it is equivalent to certain coefficient identities for operators U and D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axiom (D3): cover-pair symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: For s,t ∈ P, s ≠ t, if exactly j elements are covered by both s and t, then exactly j elements cover both s and t. (Note: j can only be 0 or 1.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures a symmetry in how pairs interact across ranks; in lattices this is equivalent to modularity. Minimality argument shows j ∈ {0,1}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflection-extension construction Ω_r(P) and rank recurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: Given P r-differential up to rank n, the reflection extension Ω_r(P) adjoins new elements (a reflection of rank n into rank n+1) to produce an r-differential poset up to rank n+1; the rank sizes satisfy p_{n+1} = r p_n + p_{n-1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iteration Ω_r^∞ on the one-element poset yields the r-Fibonacci differential poset Z_r; for r=1 the rank sizes are Fibonacci numbers ( #(Z_1)_n = F_{n+1} ). Figures illustrate the construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples: product and Young's lattice
rubrics_metrics.description: If P is r-differential and Q is s-differential then P × Q is (r + s)-differential. Young's lattice Y = J_f(N^N) is a 1-differential poset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Young's lattice verification: (D1) clear, (D3) follows from distributivity/modularity, (D2) shown by alternation of add/remove-square positions on partition boundary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vector space KP and continuity for linear transformations
rubrics_metrics.description: KP denotes the vector space (or space of infinite linear combinations) with basis P. A linear map ϕ: KP → KP is continuous if it preserves infinite linear combinations, i.e., ϕ(∑_t c_t t) = ∑_t c_t ϕ(t) whenever the right-hand side is well-defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuity is required because P may be infinite; maps not defined on basis elements or producing ill-defined infinite sums are not continuous and cannot be extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Up and Down operators U and D on KP
rubrics_metrics.description: Define continuous linear transformations U: KP → KP and D: KP → KP by U(s) = ∑_{t : t ⋗ s} t and D(s) = ∑_{t : t ⋖ s} t for each s ∈ P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These operators add (U) or remove (D) covers and are the principal algebraic tools connecting poset combinatorics to linear algebra; restrictions to finite-rank subspaces are often considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator characterization of r-differential poset (DU − UD = rI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition: P satisfying (D1) is r-differential (i.e., satisfies (D2) and (D3)) if and only if the operators U and D satisfy DU − UD = r I (I the identity on KP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives an exact linear-algebraic criterion equivalent to the combinatorial axioms; proofs compare coefficients of basis elements in the operator products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation DP = (U + r)P
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 3.21.4: For an r-differential poset P, DP = (U + r)P (as an identity on the vector with all basis elements summed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent to axiom (D2); used in enumerative derivations and exponential-operator manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator exponential identities (Theorem 3.21.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If DU − UD = rI then e^{(U+D)x} = e^{(1/2) r x^2 + U x} e^{D x}. More generally, for suitable power series f(U), D f(U) = r f'(U) + f(U) D, and e^{D x} f(U) = f(U + r x) e^{D x}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These noncommutative 'Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff–style' identities let one transfer calculations to the model U = z, D = r d/dz and are the basis for many enumerative consequences (Hasse-walk counts, generating functions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed Hasse-walk count: κ_{2n} = (2n−1)!! r^n (Theorem 3.21.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an r-differential poset P let κ_ℓ be number of Hasse walks of length ℓ from ˆ0 to ˆ0; then κ_{2n} = (2n−1)!! r^n and κ_ℓ = 0 for odd ℓ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived by applying the exponential operator identity to ⟨(U+D)^{2n} ˆ0, ˆ0⟩ and equating coefficients; shows closed-walk counts depend only on r and length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saturated-chain count: e(t)^2 = r^n n! (Theorem 3.21.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: For t in rank n of an r-differential poset, let e(t) be number of saturated chains from ˆ0 to t; then sum_{t∈Pn} e(t)^2 = r^n n!.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence of operator identities; used in further enumerative formulas and orthogonality-type computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exponential generating-function identities for level sums (Theorem 3.21.9 & 3.21.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: For r-differential P one has identities such as ⟨e^{D x} P, ·⟩ = e^{r x + (1/2) r x^2 + U x}P and the generating function ∑_n α(0→n) x^n/n! = e^{r x + (1/2) r x^2}, where α(0→n) = ∑_{t∈Pn} e(t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These concrete exponential generating functions give closed-form enumerations (e.g., α(0→n) equals the number of involutions in S_n when r=1); proofs use the operator exponential identities and pairings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank-to-rank generating series and rationality (Theorem 3.21.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed k, the generating series ∑_{n≥0} α(n→n+k) q^n equals A_k(q) F(P,q) where F(P,q)=∑_{t∈P} q^{ρ(t)} and A_k(q) is a rational function given via an explicit functional equation G(q,x)=e^{r x + (1/2) r x^2} G(q,qx) with G(q,0)=F(P,q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a method to compute α(n→n+k) from F(P,q) and shows the coefficients for fixed k are governed by a rational function in q (and r).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectrum of level-adjacency matrix (Theorem 3.21.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be the adjacency matrix of the bipartite graph formed by ranks P_{j} and P_{j+1}. Then the eigenvalues of A (over C) are 0 (with multiplicity p_j − p_{j−1}), and ±√(r s) for s=1..j with prescribed multiplicities (the theorem gives exact multiplicities in terms of rank sizes p_i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses operator relations Di+1 Ui − Ui Di = r Ii and the semidefiniteness of Ui−1 Di; yields explicit eigenvalue multiplicities and underlies counting closed walks via spectral traces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed-walk counts in level subgraph (Corollary 3.21.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix j≥1. The number of closed walks of length 2m>0 in the bipartite graph P_{j,j+1} (beginning and ending in P_j) equals ∑_{s=1}^j (p_j^{(s)} − p_{j−1}^{(s)})(r s)^m (formula derived from spectral decomposition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from trace(A^{2m}) and the spectral description of A; used to relate combinatorial walk counts to rank-size differences and powers of r.
